content:
Ashwin Rao: Heads-up — customer ACCT-942 reporting intermittent 503s right after we rotated their API key in Vault EU. They said ~10% of requests return 503 with x-request-id, and errors started ~15m after rotation. Repro steps below.

Liam Park: can you paste the request logs + sample x-request-id? curious if this is 401->503 spike or pure 503.

Ashwin Rao: sample x-request-id: req_eu_01F2KZQ7
Ashwin Rao: Here's the simplified repro they used:
```
# rotate key in Vault
vault kv put secret/redwood/apikeys/prod customer_key=<new>
# restart sidecar? they said they didn't restart anything
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotated-key>" https://inference.eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Maya Chen: hmmm. Customer on older sidecar (v0.9.4) + nginx proxy with long keepalive. We've seen long-lived connections hold old creds in header-based auth before.

Evelyn Torres: Confirmed they use sidecar-envvar-refresh: off, so env var reload won't auto-propagate unless sidecar restarts. But we also have connection pool sticky behavior in the edge LB.

Liam Park: Do we have correlation between x-forwarded-for + backend pod ip? If client connection is reused to the same backend process that didn't reload env, it could keep serving 503 if our auth-checker does a quick reject path.

ops-bot: Incident lookup: case=ACCT-942, region=eu-west-1, rotation_ts=1768803600, customer-sidecar-version=0.9.4

Ashwin Rao: I pulled the logs from their edge LB for req_eu_01F2KZQ7:
```
2026-03-15T14:18:10Z lb-eu-7 nginx: conn_id=2345 keepalive=1 backend=10.2.4.11 "POST /v1/generate" 503 125 "x-request-id=req_eu_01F2KZQ7"
2026-03-15T14:18:10Z svc-auth 10.2.4.11 "auth_check" result=key_revoked cached=true
2026-03-15T14:18:10Z svc-router 10.2.4.11 route=generate backend_pool=pool-a
```

Maya Chen: "cached=true" stands out — looks like our in-process cache of token validity didn't refresh when rotation happened. Known issue in sidecar v0.9.x where vault-watch isn't enabled by default.

Liam Park: Could also be HTTP keepalive between proxy and backend preventing new auth handshake. If the backend had the old key cached and vault returned "revoked" for new key, the flow could produce 503s for a subset of connections.

Evelyn Torres: Action plan for now: ask customer to restart sidecar (fast) or rotate at edges + flush connection pools. Longer-term: enable vault push/notify or reduce token TTL and make sidecar watch KV.

Ashwin Rao: Customer tried a restart but said traffic didn't drop — we asked for a redeploy of app to force all workers to pick up new env and reload connections. They can do that during their maintenance window.

Liam Park: For immediate mitigation we can also whitelist a graceful fallback: fallback to the old key for a few minutes during a rotation window while connections drain. But that has security implications.

Maya Chen: Dev note: add an endpoint to force connection pool flush on sidecar: `POST /_admin/flush-conns` (auth'ed). Short-term patch target for v0.9.5.

Ashwin Rao: For support reply — suggested run commands for customer:
```
# check for stale keepalives on their LB
sudo ss -tnpa | grep ESTAB | grep 10.2.4.11
# restart sidecar on one host (can do rolling)
systemctl restart redwood-sidecar
# optional: curl admin flush if available
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9900/_admin/flush-conns
```

support-bot: Suggested KB article: "Handling API key rotation when using long-lived connections and sidecars" (link internal).

Evelyn Torres: Also flagged upstream: eng-runtime ticket RT-928 to add vault-kv watch + push and decrease default keepalive for proxy-to-backend to 30s.

Liam Park: Follow-up ask to customer: can you confirm if they have any CDN or internal reverse proxies caching Authorization header? If so, need to purge.

Ashwin Rao: customer confirmed CDN (fastly) in front of LB. They purged and redeployed; error rate dropped to ~0.2% from 9% within 10m. Will monitor for next 1h and then close.

Maya Chen: Added repro notes to internal runbook: rotation can cause partial outage if (a) sidecar doesn't watch Vault, (b) proxy keeps long keepalive pools, (c) CDN caches auth headers or edge caches sticky upstream. Include mitigation checklist.

Ashwin Rao: marking this thread for postmortem if it reoccurs. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
